Relativistic effects on RCS arise from changes in incident electromagnetic field vectors due to constant velocity motion.
The Doppler effect changes frequency, but this paper focuses on field vector changes and their impact on RCS.
Lorentz transformations relate electromagnetic fields between inertial frames moving at velocity v.

The scattered fields can be expanded perturbatively in terms of velocity, with corrections proportional to v/c.
For a sphere moving at 10^3 m/s, relativistic corrections to mono-static RCS are about 10^-4 times the static RCS.
The Stewart–Tolman effect introduces an effective electric field on conduction electrons due to acceleration.

Non-uniform rotation causes the magnetic moment to depend on angular acceleration, not total acceleration.
